verdicts.quote: The Grok bot is available from inside the intended Salesforce development org.
verdicts.missing: Which surface hosts the bot (record page component, utility bar, app page, Flow action) and what context, if any, that surface passes; U-15 only says no record context is required.

verdicts.quote: The bot sends no Salesforce business-record data beyond what the user explicitly includes in the prompt.
Inspection of the outbound request shows that it contains no data drawn from the record.

Only a user with bot administration access can change the Grok connection. ... A user who can submit prompts but lacks administration access attempts to replace the credential or change the selected model. The configuration stays the same.
A user can see only outcomes belonging to their own submissions. ... neither user sees the other user's reply or failure.
A user inspecting the bot page, its browser traffic, replies and error details cannot recover the credential used by the bot.
verdicts.missing: Where the credential is stored (Named/External Credential or protected setting) and that it is kept out of code, metadata and logs.

verdicts.quote: fits within Salesforce's published cumulative timeout ceiling where an Apex callout is used.
verdicts.missing: The actual governor-limit numbers for callout timeout, callouts per transaction, heap and CPU time that bind the design.

verdicts.quote: With the provider reply delayed, the user can tell that the submission is awaiting an outcome.
verdicts.missing: The mechanism by which the interface learns the reply arrived (platform event, polled status, LMS, etc.) versus an inline return.

verdicts.quote: Repeated submit gestures for the same pending submission create only one inference request.
If the connection fails or Grok returns an HTTP 500–599 response, the user sees that Grok could not be reached or could not complete the request.
On a Grok HTTP 429 rate-limit rejection, the user sees that the service is rate limited and can try again when capacity is available.
When the service returns answer text with a confirmed output-limit truncation, the user can tell that the visible answer is incomplete.
The bot provides no saved transcript.
verdicts.missing: Whether any request record exists (e.g. for pending status, attribution or de-duplication) and, if so, its fields: role, text, status, timestamps, model identifier, usage counts.

verdicts.quote: The bot provides no saved transcript. ... A saved transcript adds a data-retention feature beyond the requested interaction.
A standalone question needs only the submitted prompt, so access to the bot does not become a route for automatic CRM disclosure.
An inspection of the Grok request for a follow-up finds zero earlier prompts or replies included as conversational context.
An otherwise valid prompt exactly at the published maximum is accepted for submission.
An administrator with access to two eligible Grok text models can change the selection and confirm that a new inference uses the newly selected model.
verdicts.missing: A switch to turn the bot off (other than revoking access or rollback) and a place where the administrator can see failed requests.

verdicts.quote: Bot setup is scoped to the designated development org.
verdicts.missing: How configuration and credential differ per environment, the deployment method (scratch org/sandbox, metadata deploy) and the production code-coverage requirement.

verdicts.quote: With no final response from Grok, the bot leaves the pending state no later than 120 seconds after accepting the submission.
A pending submission has a visible pending state.
verdicts.missing: That the empty, loading, error and refused states are deliberately designed rather than unstyled scaffolding; the states are named but no design standard is set.

verdicts.quote: Before and after use, the org's business records have the same values and membership, even when a prompt asks the bot to create, update or delete a record.
